title: Strict henselization as a limit
statement:
Let $K$ be a field, $X$ a scheme of finite type over $K$, and $x\in X$
a point with $\operatorname{trdeg}_K\kappa(x)=a>0$; put
$d=\kundim_xX$ and $X'=\Spec\bigl(\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{X,x}\bigr)$,
the strict henselization of [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit].
Then there is a separably closed field $L\supseteq K$
([def-kun-separably-closed]) and a presentation

$$
X'=\varprojlim_iX_i
$$

of $X'$ as an inverse limit of affine schemes $X_i$ of finite type over
$L$ with affine transition morphisms and
$\kundim X_i<\kundim X$ for every $i$.
(*Source:* the case of Stacks Project,
[Tag `0F0U`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F0U) that is
used in this chapter, namely the presentation of the strict henselization as a
limit of smaller-dimensional finite type models. In the Stacks Project the
proof uses Noether normalization, Algebra, Lemma 10.115.5,
[Tag `00OZ`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00OZ)
(available in this manuscript as thm:zl-relative-noether), a finite endomorphism of affine space putting the image of $x$ at the generic point of the
linear subspace, the description of the strict henselization as the filtered
colimit of the pointed etale neighbourhoods
([def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]), and the dimension bound for
an algebra which is quasi-finite over a polynomial ring.)

proof.text: Choose a geometric point $\bar x$ above $x$ for the strict henselization in the statement. The integer $a$ is finite by [lem-kun-finite-type-residue-trdeg]. Apply [lem-kun-strict-local-algebraic-residue-models] with $Y=X$ and $y=x$. It supplies an affine open neighbourhood $U$ of $x$, a separably closed field extension $L/K$ with $\operatorname{trdeg}_K L=a$, and a small cofiltered inverse system of nonempty affine schemes $X_i$ of finite type over $L$, with affine transition maps, whose limit over $U$ is $X'$. For each $i$, the map $f_i:X_i\to U$ is a $K$-morphism and $\kappa(v)/\kappa(f_i(v))$ is algebraic for every $v\in X_i$. No assertion that $f_i$ is of finite type over $K$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 0F0U, lemma-strictly-henselian, compatible etale-algebra models and the filtered-triples footnote; residue-field refinement as in the cited model node

proof.text:
Fix $i$ and a nonempty irreducible closed subset $C\subseteq |X_i|$. By [lem-sc-scheme-sober] it has a generic point $\eta$. Put $u=f_i(\eta)$ and $D=\overline{\{u\}}$ in $U$. This is nonempty and irreducible: two open sets meeting the closure of a point both contain that point, hence have nonempty intersection there. Apply [lem-sc-closed-irreducible-dimension-trdeg] to $(X_i,L,C,\eta)$ and $(U,K,D,u)$. These give $\dim C=\operatorname{trdeg}_L\kappa(\eta)$ and $\dim D=\operatorname{trdeg}_K\kappa(u)$. The $K$-morphism $f_i$ makes $K\subseteq\kappa(u)\subseteq\kappa(\eta)$ a compatible field tower; step 1 says its last extension is algebraic. Applying [lem-kun-transcendence-degree-tower] first to that tower and then to $K\subseteq L\subseteq\kappa(\eta)$ gives
$$\dim C+a=\operatorname{trdeg}_K\kappa(\eta)=\operatorname{trdeg}_K\kappa(u)=\dim D\leq\kundim U\leq\kundim X.$$
Here the inequalities follow directly from the chain definition [def-kun-dimension]: chains in the closed subspace $D$ are chains in $U$; taking closures in $X$ sends a strict chain of irreducible closed subsets of the open subspace $U$ to a strict chain in $X$, because intersecting each closure with $U$ recovers the original subset.

source.place: Tag 0B1C, item-dimension-irreducible-trdeg of lemma-dimension-locally-algebraic; trdeg_add_eq:546-550; an explicit alternative dimension calculation for the models of step 1

proof.text: By [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type], $N=\kundim X$ is finite; it is a nonnegative integer since $x\in X$. For any chain $C_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq C_r$ of nonempty irreducible closed subsets in $X_i$, the same chain in $C_r$ gives $r\leq\dim C_r$ by [def-kun-dimension]. Step 2 gives $r+a\leq N$. Since $X_i$ is nonempty, the length-zero chain obtained from the closure of any point first gives $a\leq N$. Thus every chain has length at most $N-a$, and taking the supremum gives $\kundim X_i\leq N-a<N$, because $a>0$. Combining this bound for every $i$ with the field, affineness, transition maps, and inverse-limit identification of step 1 proves the statement.
